issues.description: Visibility mismatch for two elements: (1) Farm.addAnimal(Animal) and (2) Animal(String) constructor. In the problem statement UML the members are marked with '-' (private): Farm.addAnimal is shown as private (problem_statement.md UML line showing "- addAnimal(animal: Animal):void") and the Animal constructor is shown as private (problem_statement.md UML line showing "- Animal(String): void"). In the template and usage the API is expected to be public: Main.java (template) calls farm.addAnimal(...) which requires a public addAnimal, the template Farm.java contains a TODO for implementing public farm functionality, and the solution implements public addAnimal(Animal) (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java lines 23-25) and a public Animal(String) constructor (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Animal.java lines 6-8). This inconsistency between the UML visibility markers and the intended public API can mislead students into implementing incorrect access modifiers (making methods/constructors private) which would either prevent code from compiling with the provided Main usage or lead to failing tests.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the UML visibility with the textual instructions and solution: change the UML markers from '-' to '+' for Farm.addAnimal(animal: Animal) and for Animal(String) constructor so they are shown as public. Alternatively, add a clear note in the problem statement that UML visibility markers are not authoritative and that addAnimal and the Animal constructor must be implemented as public to match the intended API and Main usage.
